references.text: Solomon acknowledges that the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, reflecting Deuteronomy's description of God's dominion over the heavens and the heaven of heavens.
The psalm declares that the earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord, echoing the same theme of God's ownership over creation.
Heaven and earth belong to the Lord; he has established them - the same theme of God's sovereign ownership.
The heaven of heavens belongs to the Lord, but he has given the earth to mankind - expanding on the relationship between God's ownership and human stewardship.
Melchizedek blesses Abram by God Most High, owner of heaven and earth.
Ezra confesses that the Lord alone created the heavens, the heaven of heavens with all their host, the earth and everything in it.
Paul quotes that the earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord, applying this to Christian freedom.
Paul proclaims in Athens that God, who made the world and everything in it, is Lord of heaven and earth.
